screens.prompt: In B10, count only the rows whose unit value is a number.

hints.syntax: =COUNT(B2:B9): one range, and the function decides what counts.
hints.func-count: COUNT counts numbers. COUNTA counts anything that is not empty.
hints.require-ref: Pass the units column from the grid rather than a typed list of quantities.
hints.value: Six rows hold a number. One cell is blank, one holds n/a, and neither is a number.
hints.error: COUNTA over the same range answers 7, because the n/a counts as a value.

reject.why: everything that is not empty counts, including the n/a text — 7
the item column is counted instead of the units
the item column holds text, so COUNT answers 0
the range starts on row 3, so the first Bolt drops out and answers 5
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the range is outside the parentheses
the right function with a stray +1, which answers 7

screens.prompt: In B10, count the rows that have an item but no numeric unit value.

hints.syntax: =COUNTA(A2:A9)-COUNT(B2:B9): every row, minus the rows with a number.
hints.func-counta: COUNTA counts rows rather than values, which is how the item column is read.
hints.func-count: COUNT supplies the half that holds real numbers.
hints.require-ref: Start both ranges on row 2 so the header never enters either count.
hints.value: Eight items and six numbers leave two rows without a quantity.
hints.error: A range that starts on row 1 counts the header as an item, which reports three.

reject.why: the count of numbers alone — six — says nothing about the missing ones
all eight items, with the numeric ones still counted
counting non-empty unit cells only finds the n/a row, which answers 1
the item column holds no numbers, so the difference is the whole 8
the ranges start on row 3, so the header row is dropped and the offset shifts
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!

docs.syntax: =COUNT(range) counts numbers; =COUNTA(range) counts anything not empty
docs.explain:
The count family answers questions that read alike. COUNT counts numbers and passes over text and blanks. COUNTA counts every cell that holds anything, so a text value enters where it would not enter a sum.

The units column holds six numbers, a blank in B4 and the text n/a in B6, so COUNT returns 6 and COUNTA returns 7. Column A holds eight items, and eight minus six leaves the 2 rows where the item exists and the quantity does not.

That subtraction is how you screen an import before trusting a total. When COUNTA and COUNT agree, every row carries a number. When they do not, the gap is the count of rows to fix.

errors.text: COUNTA over B2:B9 answers 7, because the n/a counts as a value.
COUNT over a column that holds only text answers 0 and points at nothing.
A misspelled name such as COUNTT is not a function, and Excel says so.

docs.atWork: Checking how many rows of an import carry a real quantity before a pivot or a total is trusted.
docs.outcome: Tell counting values from counting rows, then use both together to find gaps.
docs.teaches: COUNT and COUNTA, and subtracting one from the other to find gaps
docs.dataset: Parts list with a quantity column holding two gaps

seo.title: COUNT and COUNTA in Excel: the difference
seo.description: COUNT counts numbers and skips text; COUNTA counts every cell that is not empty. Subtract one from the other and you have the number of rows with a gap.
